- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days).
- Forecast tends to peak too early after sharp price spikes, then overshoots and fails to correct downward.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized — model holds high forecasts longer than actual price declines suggest.
- Late forecast days (last 5–10) show underestimation, possibly due to lagging data or model inertia.
- When history shows strong downward momentum, model fails to adjust forecast downward quickly enough.
- Forecast exhibits “sticky” behavior — fails to respond to sudden drops or spikes in recent history.
- Model overreacts to recent volatility, leading to exaggerated peaks or troughs in forecast.
- Forecast mean is typically 5–10% higher than true outcome, especially in mid-to-late forecast horizon.
- Model underestimates price recovery after sharp declines, often missing the “bounce-back” phase.
- Forecast horizon-specific bias: 1–3 day forecasts are most overconfident; 20+ day forecasts are most underconfident.
